_readme: GENERATED by `python3 -m tools.blueprint build` — never hand-edit. This is the orientation map for an agent opening this repository cold: read blueprint/SYSTEM.md FIRST, then open only the files it points at. Every value here is derived from the artifact that owns it; nothing is restated.

How This Engine Analyzes a Contract

open_work.title: The native chart kinds (bar, pie, radar, heat map, timeline, sankey, geo map, isometric, layered workflow) do not carry the per-mark attribute contract
Rung 2 tests "contents are enumerable" by counting PUBLIC top-level definitions, which under-reads a delegation shim
`CHANGELOG.md` is structurally exempt from the `counts` guard
The depth ratchet constrains a container's DEPTH, never its CONTENTS
The completeness report's `changelog` step, and any claim that a named gate does the job it is credited with, cannot be checked mechanically
A body-certifying stamp certifies `verified` from a dangling, unpublished commit, so `verified` is machine-local
No minimum Python version is enforced, so an old interpreter produces a self-consistently WRONG map
The gatekeeper relation still cannot see a gate that reaches a module by GLOB rather than by import or name
`SURFACES.md` §1 covers only `argparse` entry points, so the node and shell ones are absent
docgen's dependency-graph renderer cannot draw a graph this dense: straight edges cross non-endpoint nodes
`docs/archive/` and `docs/archives/_trash` differ by one letter and mean opposite things
The archive certifies itself: body, snapshot and recorded sha256 can be forged in lockstep
CI was not wired to the VPS2 self-hosted runner
`L17` and `L22` are unallocated
`L20` (brand manifest) has no bundled artifact
`DESIGN_SYSTEM.md` and `calibration/*` are absent
`_GATE_TO_CONTRADICTION_TOKENS` is data living in code
Risks **R1–R6** live in `PROVENANCE.md`, not here
The secret gate depends on a scanner outside the repo
The `host_root()` migration is incomplete in several modules
Nothing reads the docgen JSON Schema files
`CONS-03` raises the cost of unlocking a rule file without removing self-certification
Mermaid SVG relies on `color-mix()` and CSS custom properties
"`tools.health` exits 0 printing nothing if a check raises"
`--full` turns `STRUCT-06`'s deliberate SKIP into a failure
"The ECharts pie renders empty when one slice is 100%"
An EBCDIC (cp037/cp500) classified document walks past the commit-time placement gate
The depth-ratchet's history memory hardcodes SHA-1 (40-hex); a SHA-256 repository reads as "no history"
A committed ratchet LOOSENING is undetected when the ratchet is run in a shallow / partial / grafted clone
`SUITE-07` and the refuse-empty guard cover only 2 of the 5 graphify builders
`layout --check` has a blind spot for an orphaned `system.layout.svg` while the layout is unclean
The blueprint layer's dependency graph reads **Python only**, so a non-Python host project gets no derived module map

system.name: Ultimate Engine
system.purpose: A documentation engine with a governance layer: it turns authored Markdown into design-system HTML with deterministic, sourced figures, and enforces a rule layer over the corpus. This repository is also its own first test corpus (docs/CHARTER.md).

containers.name: The document engine
containers.purpose: Parse a Markdown document and its sidecar figures, adjudicate it against the rule layer, render it to design-system HTML/SVG/PDF, and refuse to write anything a blocking gate rejected.

containers.name: The git moat
containers.purpose: Content gates installed into .git/hooks: classification placement and a secret scan over the index at commit time, and over every commit in the pushed range at push time.

containers.name: The corpus checker
containers.purpose: Run the guard set over this repository's own tracked documents, so a stale count, a dead citation, a present-tense plan or a contradicting register row fails a check instead of waiting for a verification pass to find it by hand.

containers.name: The health run
containers.purpose: The single entry point that runs every gate in one command — structure, rule layer, cross-file consistency, build, and both npm suites — and never reports a SKIP as a pass.

containers.name: The blueprint layer
containers.purpose: Derive the system map an agent reads INSTEAD of the tree, verify the committed copy against a fresh derivation, and build the gitignored SQLite index that answers joins over it.

containers.name: The draft gate
containers.purpose: Splice a candidate document into a throwaway copy of the working tree and report the DIFFERENCE it would introduce — including findings that land on other documents because this one moved a fact they state.

containers.name: The project census
containers.purpose: Measure a project's documentation system from its own git tree (documents, freshness, what is crossed out, stamps and whether they hold, completeness by dimension) and its Python code hierarchy, then compose them into a report of varied figures and two explorers. Reads git and writes only where told; composes the document, chart and Mermaid engines without changing them.

containers.name: The artifact index
containers.purpose: Enumerate the project's registered artifacts and render the browsable dashboard over them.

containers.name: Shared primitives
containers.purpose: The primitives more than one container depends on — chiefly the ONE Markdown table reader, which replaced five readers measured disagreeing on the manifest's own header cell.

containers.name: The retained counter-examples
containers.purpose: Every assertion this engine makes about itself, retained as a probe that was shown RED before it was trusted. Run by the health suite on every pass.

schemas.title: DocHeader
schemas.describes: The required document metadata header (RULEBOOK L5; CLASSIFICATION.md). Mirrors tools/docgen/models.py DocHeader.

schemas.title: DocManifestRows
schemas.describes: A serialized list of DOC_MANIFEST.md rows (tools/docgen/models.py ManifestRow), as read_manifest() would emit if dumped to JSON. Used to validate manifest-derived data passed between tools.

schemas.title: ExportManifest
schemas.describes: Written by every export/render pass (CLASSIFICATION.md leak-gate item 5). Records per-file hashes and the verifier-stamp; a missing stamp or created_at blocks release.

schemas.title: VisualSpec
schemas.describes: A renderable diagram specification (VISUAL_LIBRARY.md; MOTION_SPEC.md). Mirrors tools/docgen/models.py VisualSpec/Node/Edge/LegendEntry/DataSource.

commands.help: build a Markdown document into HTML/JSON/PDF
flags: --allow-rulebook-drift — Build even when the RULEBOOK L9 hash-gate is blocking. Never use for a source-of-truth artifact — it disables the locked-rule guard for this run.

--cache — path to an incremental build-cache JSON. When set, an unchanged document (same source, sibling spec, formats, flag, and engine) whose outputs still exist is skipped. Fail-open: a corrupt/absent cache just does a full build.

--cached — build through the conventional incremental cache: <out-dir>/.docgen_cache.json, or .docgen/.docgen_cache.json when no -o is given. An unchanged document whose outputs still exist is skipped. Use --cache PATH to name the file explicitly. Ignored under --strict, which always re-runs the gate.
--formats — comma-separated formats: html,json,blueprint,pdf (default: html); blueprint = the AI-only <stem>.blueprint.json twin of the document

--local-preview — allow a CONFIDENTIAL/SECRET document to render for local review (Gate 1 relaxed to advisory); out-dir must resolve under docs/confidential/ or the build is blocked. Never affects a public document. Never makes a doc export-eligible.
--watch — rebuild on a fixed interval until interrupted (poll-based, stdlib-only). Combine with --cached or --cache so unchanged ticks are near-free.
input — path(s) to the source .md file(s). Several paths build as one corpus through a single shared cache (one cache load, one engine fingerprint, one save).

global_flags: --manifest — Scan (blob-sha<TAB>path) records read from FILE, fetching each blob with `git cat-file`. Used by pre-push over the objects being published, so placement is enforced on what is PUBLISHED — `git merge`, `git cherry-pick` and `git rebase` all create commits without pre-commit — and read blob-true, which a directory walk cannot be.

--repo-root — Repository root to scan. Default: the CWD's git root, falling back to this file's location — see `_repo_root_default`. Whatever this resolves to is the repository whose blobs are read AND whose ignore rules decide the vault anchor; the two used to be able to disagree.

guards.checks: ``register`` — a register must be able to name its own rows.
``crossrefs`` — every internal link and document reference must resolve.
``symbols`` — a backticked identifier must exist in the source tree, or be marked planned.
``test-refs`` — every cited test name and every cited **check id** must exist.
``counts`` — a number a document states about the system must re-derive from the system.
``identity`` — a document's version claim, checked against the bytes that would prove it.
``cross-doc`` — when two documents enumerate the same set, the sets must match.
``present-tense`` — a thing marked planned may never be described in the present tense.
``stamps`` — a stamp whose recorded commit no longer matches the file body is invalid.
``built-claims`` — a documented command must actually be runnable.
``rendered-output`` — guards run against **built artifacts too**, not only source.

to_register: add the `(GUARD, run)` pair to `GUARDS`, in the run-order position it belongs in

run `python3 -m tools.blueprint build` and commit the regenerated `blueprint/` files — the guard registry is part of the derived map, so a new guard makes it stale and the retained suite fails the push until it is rebuilt
guard_contract.cost_note: Three edits, not two. It was two until Phase 5 put the guard registry into the derived map — a verifier registered a guard with exactly the two documented edits and left the tree push-blocked, with `blueprint: STALE` on five files. The phase that invalidated the number is the phase that owes the correction.
invariants: a finding names a line — `path:line`, or `path` with line 0 for a whole-file finding
a guard reports `checked`, and a `floor` below which a clean run is a FAILURE, because a guard that examined nothing has not passed (`LESSONS.md` L-19)
SKIP is never a pass — it means the guard could not run and its question is open

health_checks.asserts: The process documents this project runs on must exist.
Every file VERSION.json locks must be on disk — the hash-gate fails closed without them.
The push-time moat (engine health + a secret scan of the pushed content) must be live.
The commit-time moat (classification placement + a secret scan of the index) must be live.
The confidential vault must be git-ignored — six places in this tree assume it is.
EVERY tracked npm lockfile must carry a sibling ``VERSION_LOCK.json`` that attests its hash.
The portfolio CI cost-control gate must actually run, and pass.
The crash-recovery record must carry a stamp that parses and points at real history.
STRUCT-08 — if the config file actually in force exists, it must parse.
The L9 rulebook hash-gate must hold: no undeclared drift in a locked rule.
CONTRADICTION.md must parse into rows — presence is not consultation.
Every documented L10 change type must resolve to a real, populated map entry.
TAXONOMY.md must yield a non-empty prefix set — an empty set blocks every document.
DOC_MANIFEST.md must yield at least one registry row.
Every prefix the L10 map tells you to review must be a real doc type.
Every DOC_MANIFEST row id must be a registered TAXONOMY prefix.
RULEBOOK.md's locked-file table must name exactly VERSION.json's rulebook_files.
CONS-10 — no governance table is split in two by a blank line.
Every gate the ENGINE EMITS must have a precedence position, and every rule gate a firing row.
PROJECT_VERSION must equal the newest version heading in CHANGELOG.md.
Every symbol a RULEBOOK Status line cites must exist in the file it names.
Repo-relative paths cited in the core process documents must exist.
The three "starting state" documents must not misstate the facts they exist to hand over.
The charter's two measured counts must be re-derived, not trusted.
CONS-11 — the corpus checker's guard set must be clean over this repository's own documents.
A real document must still build end to end.
``cli check`` must pass on EVERY tracked doc-system document, not one hardcoded sample.
No entry point may report degraded governance consultation.
BUILD-04 — the committed `themes/*.json` must equal a fresh rebuild, byte for byte.
SUITE-03 — the artifact index must resolve, over a NON-EMPTY set, and the dashboard must render every row it holds.
SUITE-01 — the visual-engine npm suite must pass AND report at least 30 passing tests.
SUITE-02 — the mermaid-engine npm suite must pass AND report at least 6 diagram types.
Lint and type-check counts must not exceed the pinned baseline.
The retained counter-examples must pass, and there must not be fewer of them than before.
The retained moat attacks must still be refused.
SUITE-07 — the graphify builders must emit a NON-EMPTY graph, not merely exit 0.
CONS-12 — the depth ratchet must be level, measured against the REAL repository.
CONS-13 — the plan's prose and its phase rows must agree about which phases are finished.
